t: Count Integers With Even Digit Sum
o: We count how many of 1, 2, ..., num have a digit sum divisible by 2. For num = 4 only 2 and 4 qualify; for num = 30 fourteen numbers qualify, namely 2, 4, 6, 8, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 20, 22, 24, 26 and 28. Because num <= 1000, testing each integer by extracting its digits is trivially fast enough. The deeper structure is that digit-sum parity follows a rigid pattern inside every block of ten: the tens contribution stays fixed while the units digit sweeps 0..9, which opens the door to an O(1) counting formula. Treat this problem as simulation practice with a math upgrade as the bonus.
k: Only the parity of the digit sum matters, not the magnitude of the number.
Within a complete decade [10j, 10j+9] the digit sums are ds(j) + b for b = 0..9, so exactly five numbers per decade have even digit sum.
With num <= 1000 a straightforward simulation is the intended solution; the decade argument yields an O(1) alternative.

a.i: Iterate x from 1 to num, peel off digits with division and modulo to accumulate the digit sum, and count x whenever that sum is even. Given the tight constraint num <= 1000 this performs at most a few thousand cheap operations. It is also the clearest, least error-prone solution.
s: For each x from 1 to num, compute its digit sum via repeated x % 10 and integer division.
Increment the counter when the digit sum is even.
a.t: O(num log num) — num integers, each processed in time proportional to its digit count.

a.i: Split [1, num] into full decades plus a partial one. Decade j covers 10j..10j+9 with digit sums ds(j) + b for b = 0..9, and among ten consecutive b values exactly five match the parity of ds(j); decade 0 contributes only four because 0 is not positive. For the partial decade d = num // 10 ending at r = num % 10, count units b in 0..r whose parity equals that of ds(d), again excluding the phantom 0 when d = 0. Everything reduces to fixed arithmetic plus one tiny digit-sum computation.
s: Let d = num // 10 and r = num % 10.
Full decades contribute 5*d - 1 when d > 0 (five per decade minus the nonpositive 0), otherwise 0.
Compute want = digit_sum(d) % 2, the required units-digit parity.
Add r//2 + 1 numbers if want is even, or (r+1)//2 if odd, then subtract 1 more when d == 0 and want == 0.
a.t: O(1) — fixed arithmetic plus one digit-sum computation over at most four digits.

w: Lead with the simulation — under num <= 1000 it is the right engineering trade-off, and it doubles as a correctness oracle if you also show the O(1) decade trick. Pitfalls live almost entirely in the math version: forgetting that decade 0 must exclude the number 0, and mixing up the even/odd partial-decade formulas. Useful sanity anchors: countEven(1) = 0, countEven(9) = 4, countEven(30) = 14, countEven(1000) = 499. A natural follow-up is num up to 10^18, which demands digit DP or generalized positional counting rather than simulation.
